votes.refutation: Attempted refutations: (1) The single check is documented intent, not an oversight: tasks.py:1115-1116 says the task fires "after review_hog's TaskRun receiver resolved the acting reviewer and confirmed their toggle", and the carve-out docstring (tasks.py:160-165) explicitly addresses a toggle "switched off mid-PR" by relying on the skip path's stale-approval dismissal ("safety is never preference-gated"). So a post-opt-out approval is retracted on the next push; only the no-push ready-for-review flip on an unchanged head leaves the approval standing. (2) The trigger window is normally seconds (receiver on_commit -> Celery -> GitHub fetch); it only stretches to minutes under GitHub rate limiting or Temporal outages, which are rare. (3) The suggested fix does not close the race: the Temporal review workflow itself runs for minutes after the task and also never re-checks the toggle before `post_approve_review`, so check-at-task-start only narrows the window marginally rather than "to zero" as the finding claims. Net: the defect is real (toggle not re-read at execution, inconsistent with the webhook leg), but it is bounded by the later-push retraction, documented as the leg's design, and the proposed fix is a cheap consistency hardening rather than a must-ship correctness fix. The reviewer's should_fix overstates it; the validator's `consider` is the right level.

Reachability in production configuration (all paths under /Users/woutut/.worktrees/posthog/frozen-75215):

No feature flag gates any of this; CodeReviewScene.tsx:1548 says `FEATURE_FLAGS.REVIEW_HOG` only controls menu visibility.

2. The toggle is user-writable in prod: `stamphog_review_inbox_prs` is a plain BooleanField on ReviewUserSettings (models.py:294), exposed for write in the settings serializer (products/review_hog/backend/api/settings.py:27-32) and bound to a UI switch (CodeReviewScene.tsx:1061-1062). A user can flip it at any time.

3. The toggle is read exactly twice in the whole tree: receivers.py:126 (the one-shot receiver check before `_start_stamphog_review`) and receivers.py:154 inside `resolve_stamphog_acting_reviewer`, which is only invoked via `get_inbox_acting_reviewer_resolver()` from the webhook carve-out at products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:201-205. `process_inbox_pr_review` (tasks.py:1109-1245) resolves the repo config, fetches the PR, and creates the ReviewRun with `output={"inbox_review": ...}` (tasks.py:1176-1230) and never consults the resolver or the toggle; `acting_user_id` is stamped as trusted provenance only.

4. The verdict step then posts a real approval via `client.post_approve_review` (activities.py:745).

5. The window is not seconds: Celery pickup -> GitHub fetch with `max_retries=3` and a rate-limit countdown of `max(retry_after, 60)` (tasks.py:1160-1162) -> run creation -> Temporal workflow -> sandbox clone + LLM review -> post_verdict. Realistically minutes, which is enough for "see the PR notification, go to settings, flip it off".

6. The mitigation only covers pushes: the carve-out docstring (tasks.py:160-166) states a toggle switched off mid-PR is retracted on a head-changing delivery, and that a ready_for_review flip alone keeps the draft-time approval. So opt-out followed by ready-for-review on an unchanged head leaves the approval standing.

Conclusion: the trigger is reachable in production configuration and the asymmetry with the webhook leg is real. Severity stays at consider rather than should_fix: the single check is documented as the intended contract (tasks.py:1115-1116, facade/api.py:138-139), the user had consented at trigger time, any later push self-heals, and the suggested re-check inside the task only narrows the race (a flip after the re-check but before `post_approve_review` at activities.py:745 has the same outcome). It is a cheap consistency hardening, not a shipping defect.
